out.why: Care for the baby, then tend the Hart field and gather firewood/food in rain.
Care for the baby, then milk the cows and gather firewood/wild food to keep the household fed in the rain.
Rain, summer. Baby needs care daily. Care for Basilia, then weed/hoe our West Field, and gather firewood as fallback. Food is fine for now.

Rain today but the household is well-stocked, so I'll secure land claims for the future, keep Gunnild cared for, build up food variety through trapping and foraging, and try to grow the family further with Alice. I'll also reach out about trading for grain seed since we have none to sow yet.

tell.text: Our stores are good this rainy day - I'll mind Gunnild and set traps at the Brook. Shall we try for another child tonight by the fire?
Could you help gather food or mind your sisters today while I'm at the Brook setting traps? We should keep building up our stores.
Do the Shepherds have any spare grain or seed? I'd trade coin or work for some - I want to get a field sown while the season allows.

note.title: Strategy
note.text: Day 1, summer: claimed Middle Pasture & the Leaze (2 plots each) for the Marshs, adding to our held Ham meadow. Store is strong: ~62 meals, 72 firewood, 28 timber - no immediate hunger risk. No grain/rye/beans seed on hand yet, so sowing (my trade) waits on trade or find. Set children to herd the ox. Priorities going forward: (1) keep Gunnild cared for daily - she's a baby and needs it or may die; (2) grow the family further via Alice; (3) build food variety through trapping at the Brook and wild gathering since smoked fish stock (21) is our main protein; (4) get grain seed by trade (offered 1 coin for 5 grain) so I can finally sow a field; (5) watch for when Marsh House (3 free spaces, 8 beds for 7 people) needs expansion as the children grow and more are born.

out.why: With the household growing (Lettice grown in 2 days, more children soon) and Marsh House nearly full, I'll use today's rain-bound time to tend Gunnild and start adding a room onto Marsh House using the timber already in store; any spare units go to firewood.

actions.pass: Our line is Jocelin and Alice Marsh's; help it grow and spread, and look after your kin.

tell.text: I'm starting an added room on Marsh House today with the store's timber - we'll need the space soon with the children growing up. I've tended Gunnild already.
It's raining - if you've a mind to, gathering wild food or firewood today would help the stores while I work on the new room.

note.title: Family plan
note.text: Day 1/4(of4) summer rain. Started adding a small room to Marsh House (needs ~4.5 units total, 6 timber, drawn from the 28 in store) to house the growing family - Lettice grown in 2 days, Letice in 5, Everard in 7, Gunnild in 9. Stores healthy: 62.6 meals, ~92 nights fuel. Next: consider clearing a field for grain, or expanding food variety via trapping/netting (my skilled crafts) once housing is sorted. Watch for more children needing beds.

tell.text: Rain's set in for the day, good a day as any to stay close by the hearth - let's try for another child tonight, after the work's done.
Our bins have no grain or seed at all this year - only coin and a tool to offer. Do the Brooks have any grain to spare, or know where seed might be had before sowing season's gone?
Do the Shepherds have grain or seed to spare? We've coin, or a crude tool, to trade for some - we've none in our own store.

note.title: Seed Grain
note.text: Marsh House store holds no grain, rye or beans - nothing to sow. Only coin and a crude tool to trade for seed. Watch for anyone passing with grain to spare, or send word to Middleham/Lowstrand households, who grow barley. Until seed is had, the Ham, Middle Pasture and the Leaze can still be cut for hay, and the scrub fields gathered or hunted over.

note.title: Growth Plan
note.text: Goal: grow the line as many generations and as many descendants as possible by day 200. Keep trying for children with Alice while both are of age (she turns elder day ~29 from founding). Raise the children well, pass on the goal to each. As the household grows, add rooms/beds at Marsh House (small room: 6 timber, 4.5 units added). When grown children are ready, consider founding new households or claiming land to spread the line rather than crowding one house. Keep food store well above need - last winter's stores ran out, don't repeat that.

out.why: It's a rainy day with a comfortable store (62.6 meals, fuel for ~92 nights), so nothing is urgent except keeping Gunnild cared for and pushing on the one thing that matters most for my real goal: more children and more generations. I'll spend 1 unit caring for Gunnild (critical for a baby), put 2 units into trying for another child with Alice tonight, and use the rest gathering wild food at Hazel Copse to keep our diet varied and our stores growing rather than just coasting on what we have. I'm setting the children to forage as their small daily task so even they add a little to the larder. We have no seed grain at all in store, which will stop us sowing anything this season unless we trade for some - so I'm quietly asking Lambert and Baldwin whether their households have grain or seed to spare for our coin or a crude tool, and leaving an open offer for anyone passing through. I'm attending to the Ham today, since it's our own meadow and I want to know it well before deciding whether to mow it for hay or try sowing it once we have seed. Building a new room can wait - we still have 3 free spaces and the family won't outgrow the house for several more days yet; better to spend today's effort on the baby, on trying for another child, and on food, which matter more right now.

Today I prioritize growing our line: trying for another child with Sabina since we only have about 20 days before becoming elders, coordinating with my sons to seek partners so they can start having children, setting fish traps for passive food gathering overnight, and gathering firewood with remaining time.

tell.text: Wife, I plan to try for another child with you tonight. We have only about 20 days before we become elders and can no longer have children.
Son, you are grown now. You should seek a partner and start having children. Our line depends on many descendants.
Son, you should also seek a partner soon. The more children and grandchildren we have, the stronger our line becomes.

out.why: With only 20 days before Sabina and I become elders, I must maximize our family's growth now. Today I'll try for another child with Sabina while encouraging Baldwin and Tobin to find partners and start their own families. I'll hunt in East Wood to replenish our dwindling food stores which currently last only 9 nights.

tell.text: Son, seek Alice of the Marshs as your partner today. If she agrees, try for a child with her tonight. We must grow our line while there is time.
Would you become partners with my son Baldwin? He is a good man who will provide well, and together you can build a strong family.
Seek a partner today - Mabel, Matilda, or one of the Marsh women. Try for a child tonight if she agrees. Our line must grow.

note.title: Family Growth Plan
note.text: URGENT: Maximize children before Sabina and I become elders in 20 days. Current tasks: Get Baldwin partnered (Alice?), get Tobin partnered (Mabel/Matilda?), prepare for Margery (grows Day 2) and Rose (grows Day 9) to find partners. Try with Sabina every 2-3 days. Food critical - 9 nights left, hunt/gather daily. Track all descendants for Day 200 goal.

tell.text: You are grown. Seek a partner from the Brooks or Marshs to start your family and continue our line. This is urgent - our success depends on all of us having children quickly.
You are grown. Seek a partner from the Brooks or Marshs to start your family and continue our line. This is urgent - our success depends on all of us having children quickly.
Tomorrow you become grown. Immediately seek a partner to start your family and grow our line. Time is precious - the more children we all have, the stronger our line becomes.

out.why: My goal is to maximize descendants by day 200. With only 20 days before I turn elder and can no longer father children, every day counts. I must continue trying for children with Sabina - using 2 units gives us a better chance. Margery becomes grown tomorrow, and with Baldwin and Tobin already grown, getting all three partnered immediately is critical. The more children they have, the more our line grows. Our food stores are adequate for now (9+ nights) but I'll gather wild food to sustain our expanding household. I'm attending to the village layout to better understand our community and potential partnerships.
Stores are thin after last winter, so today I'm bringing in food: milk from the cow, wicker traps set in the river, and wild food. I'm also trying for a child with Orabel to grow the line.

tell.text: Wife, let us try for another child tonight. We sleep at Field House as ever. Hawise, if she will, could gather wild food so we put more by for winter.

out.why: Our stores are thin for four mouths after last hard winter, so I'll milk and gather wild food into the store while summer is generous. I'll also try for a child with Orabel to grow the line.

tell.text: Let us try for another child tonight; I'll put a unit to it. Stores are thin, so I'm gathering wild food while it's plentiful.

out.why: Our stores hold about 7 nights of food for four of us, and last winter ran short. So today I'll gather what food I can: milk the cow, set the wicker traps, weed the barley so the harvest is good, and gather wild food. Orabel and I will also try for a child while we are both young enough. Drew is grown tomorrow, which gives us another pair of hands.

tell.text: Wife, let us try for another child tonight. I've set aside two units for it. Let's keep the stores close and gather what wild food we can, because winter will come hard again.

note.title: Plan
note.text: Food is short: 32 grain and 8 beans, about 7 nights. Barley is on all 6 plots of Middleham Field; reap it when ripe and keep seed back. Build up stores for winter: milk, traps, wild food, fish. Try for children with Orabel often (I turn elder at 64 days). Drew is grown on day 2 of these days.

out.why: Our field North Field Upper lies fallow and needs work. With Avice and I both aging toward our elder years, we must try for another child while we still can - this is critical to growing our line. I'll prepare the field by hoeing today, then sow soon. Naming Gervase as heir secures the household's future.

tell.text: Wife, we grow older and have little time left to bear children. Jory becomes a man tomorrow. Let us try for another child today - our line depends on it. Please try with me tonight.

out.why: With both Avice and I aging toward elderhood, we must try for more children to grow our line. Meanwhile, I'll prepare North Field Upper for autumn planting by hoeing it.

tell.text: Wife, we grow older and must secure our line. Let us try for another child tonight - our time grows short before we cannot.

out.why: My most urgent priority is growing my line. Avice and I have only 19 days before she turns elder and can bear no more children. We must try for another child starting today. Jory becomes grown tomorrow, so I'll care for him one last time. I'll milk our cow for food - milk spoils fast but adds to our stores. I should name Gervase as my heir in case anything happens to me. Our field appears unplanted but we're past optimal time for summer crops - I'll need to plan for autumn rye planting.

tell.text: Wife, we must try for another child while we still can. You turn elder in 19 days. Will you try with me today? Jory grows up tomorrow - our family can be larger yet.

note.title: Seasonal Planning
note.text: Summer day 4, 4 days left. Missed optimal planting window for barley/beans. Plan to sow RYE in LATE AUTUMN (best time). North Field Upper is our land - 7 plots. Must prepare and plant then. Meanwhile build food stores through milking and other gathering.

out.why: My line only grows if we have children and food. Lucy and I have about 18 days left to breed, so I give part of today to that; the rest to wild food for the store, since our household holds no cornfield. I claim two plots of the unheld Common to begin making one, name Matthew heir, and push my grown children to find partners here.

tell.text: Wife, I turn elder in eighteen days and you in twenty-four. Every child we get now is another Wright for all the years after. Set aside time with me today and each day while we still can, and I will keep the store filled so no babe of ours goes hungry.

You are grown, and the house will be yours after me - I have named you heir. Take a wife while there are women here to take: Avice or Idonea, or ask at Middleham. Children of yours are my whole purpose; say the word and I will stand with you in the asking and find the bride-gift.

Daughter, look at Clement, Elias or Gervase, or at the Middleham men. Choose one who works and will feed children. Stay in Lowstrand if you can; I would have your babes close by our hearth, and our store will help feed them.

Avice, my son Matthew is grown, steady, and heir to Wright House and its store. If a match between our houses would suit you or your kin, I will deal generously - grain, timber, and my own hands at your plough and your harvest.

note.title: Plan for the line
note.text: Goal: most living descendants at day 200. Levers: (1) children of my own while Lucy and I are not elder (I turn elder 18 days after day 1, Lucy 24). (2) Marry off Matthew and Wilmot here or in Middleham so they breed early. (3) Food: Wright House holds only Lowstrand Meadow, no cornfield. Claimed 2 plots of Lowstrand Common (unheld pasture) on day 1 to clear into field; also hold 2 cows+calf (H7) for milk. (4) Keep store above 34 meals; last winter the stores ran out. Wild food, fish by hand/angle, water traps and bird netting are cheap summer-autumn food. (5) Autumn: hire out my skilled reaping and sowing to the Woods and Cotters for grain.

out.why: My line is what counts, and I have only 18 days left to father children, so Lucy and I try again today. Beyond that, the Wrights hold no arable at all — only a meadow — so I claim grazing on the unclaimed Common to grow into, offer my skilled hands to the Woods and Cotters for grain, and spend the rest of a wet day gathering wild food, since our store holds barely a week of meals. I also push Matthew and Wilmot to pair off here while there are young folk in both other houses.

tell.text: Wife, I turn elder in eighteen days and you in twenty-four. Every child we get now is our line's whole future. Lie with me tonight, and keep yourself fed and out of the wet — I would rather you forage near the green than break your back in the field.

Son, hear me plainly: a man with no wife leaves nothing behind. Avice of the Cotters and Idonea of the Woods are both here and both of age. Go and work beside one of them, speak well of her house, and partner with her before the season turns. Children of yours count as Wrights to me wherever they sleep.

Daughter, the Woods and Cotters have grown men here — Elias, Clement, Gervase. Choose one who works and partner with him this season; stay in Lowstrand so your babes are near our store and our fire. I will see you want for nothing while you carry.

Clement, the Wrights hold no ploughland, and I am the best hand with a hoe, a seed-basket and a sickle in this village. Let me sow and reap two of the Woods' plots in Lowstrand Field and I will take my pay in grain at harvest — say a quarter of what those plots yield. Your house loses nothing and gains my back.

note.title: Line plan
note.text: Goal: most living descendants of Aldric and Lucy Wright by day 200. I am 46; elder (no more children) at 64. Lucy elder in 24 days. So: father children every day I can for the next 18 days. Grown children now: Matthew, Wilmot; Payn grown in 5 days. Each must be partnered young and kept fed - their children count wherever they live. Mates available: Cotters (Avice, Gervase, Warin), Woods (Clement, Elias, Idonea, Odo); more in Middleham (Fields, Fletchers, Harts) and Highpool (Brooks, Marshs, Shepherds). Weakness: Wrights hold only Lowstrand Meadow (1 plot) and cows H7 (2 cows, 1 calf). No arable. Fix by claiming Common plots and clearing to field, or by hiring my skilled hands out for grain. Store day 4 summer: 40 grain, 10 beans, 6 hen, 60 firewood, 28 timber; 5 eaters a night. Last winter was hard - build stores before autumn ends.

out.why:
My score is my living descendants on day 200, so children are everything. I am 46 days old and turn elder in 18 days; Lucy in 24. Every day from now I should be trying for another child with Lucy, and pushing Matthew and Wilmot to pair off with the Wood and Cotter young so their children come too — a grandchild counts as much as a child, and they come faster from the young.

The danger is food. Our store holds about 34 meals and we eat 5 a night: a week's grace, and we hold no cornfield at all, only one hay plot. The Woods hold Lowstrand Field and the Cotters North Field Upper. So: (1) I set the children to foraging each day, (2) I gather wild food into the bins today, (3) I offer my hands — I am skilled at hoe, weed, reap, sow, plough — to the Woods and Cotters for grain, the fastest way to turn skill into stores, and (4) over the coming days I mean to clear new ground off the Common into a field of my own, so my line is not a tenant on other men's barley forever. Today I claim two plots of the Common, where our cows already graze, as the ground to clear.

I also name Matthew heir, so the household holds together if I am taken.

tell.text: Son, you are named my heir. Hear me: the Wright name lives by children, not by barley. Speak to Idonea of the Wood house, or Avice of the Cotters - partner with one of them and get children while you are young. Your children are my line as much as you are. And learn the plough from me before I am an elder.

Daughter, look to Clement or Elias of the Wood house. Take a partner this season and have children - do not wait. Whatever house you go to, your children are Wrights by blood and I will see them fed. Come to me if either man wants a bride-gift; I will find it.

Clement, your barley on Lowstrand Field wants hoeing and weeding, and there is no better hand at it in Lowstrand than mine. Give me 15 grain and I will work two full days in your field. And I will say plainly: my daughter Wilmot is of age, and a tie between Wright and Wood would serve both our houses.

Avice, the same word to the Cotters as to the Woods: 15 grain for two days of my hands on North Field Upper - hoe, weed, reap, as you need. I am skilled at all three. And my son Matthew is grown and looking for a partner; think on it.

note.title: The line's plan
note.text: Score = living descendants alive on day 200. Rules I must not forget: 1) Try for a child with Lucy nearly every day - I turn elder in 18 days, she in 24. 2) Push Matthew and Wilmot to partner (Woods: Clement, Elias, Idonea; Cotters: Avice, Gervase) and breed early; their children count toward my line wherever they live. 3) Payn grows in 5 days - then he too must partner. 4) Food: store 34 meals, 5 eaten a night. We hold NO cornfield, only Lowstrand Meadow (1 plot) and 2 claimed plots of Lowstrand Common. Plan: clear Common into field, sow barley, and meanwhile sell my skilled hands (hoe/weed/reap/sow/plough) to Woods and Cotters for grain. 5) Children ordered to forage. 6) Heir: Matthew.

out.why: Keep the baby alive, try for another child with Mabel while we are both still young enough, and start laying in food since the store only covers about ten days.

tell.text: I will mind Matilda today. Let us try for another child tonight - put 2 units to it with me - and spend the rest gathering food; the store is only ten days deep.
Son, put your day into food for the house: fish the Brook or gather wild food. We need the store deeper before autumn.

out.why: Keep the baby alive, try for another child with Mabel while she still can, and start building the food store with traps and foraging.

tell.text: Let us try for another child today, 2 units each, and sleep at Brook House. I will care for Matilda today; you gather food for the store with the rest of your day.
Our store holds about ten days of food. Fish the Brook and gather wild food for the household today, please.

out.why: Our store feeds us about 10 days, and Mabel and I have about 20 days left to have more children. Today I care for the baby, try for a child with Mabel, and start bringing in food with water traps and foraging. Further ahead: build up food before autumn, get Saer partnered, and add beds as the family grows.

tell.text: Let us try for another child tonight: put 2 units to it with me. I will mind Matilda today; spend the rest of your day gathering food for our store.
Son, fish or forage for the household today; our store is only ten days deep. And look for a wife among the Marshs or Shepherds, our line must grow.
